Retractable ratchet straps: This is your product. Use these ads as a benchmark for hooks, offers and how long a winning strap ad runs.
Windproof tarp clips: Same buyer as your straps: anyone tying down a load on a ute or trailer. Small, cheap to post, easy add-on or bundle (straps + tarp clips).
Anti-rattle hitch tightener: Sells to the same towing crowd. Small, light, and an easy upsell at checkout next to straps.
Electric trailer dolly: Same trailer and boat owners, but high price and heavy freight. A bigger step up in stock and shipping cost.
Ute dash phone/tablet mount: Same ute owners, but brand-name mounts already own this in AU.
Concrete FormExtenders: Different buyer (concreters), sold trade-to-trade. Opens a new customer group rather than adding to your.
Concrete step repair adhesive: Homeowner DIY buyer, not your tradie customer. Chemical shipping rules add hassle.
Concrete chainsaw (ICS): Big-ticket machinery for specialist contractors. Very different business from straps.
Boulder Buddy rock lifter: Landscapers and machinery owners. Overlaps if your buyers run machines or trailers for landscaping.
Clamp-on pallet forks: Farm and machinery owners who also haul with trailers. Heavy freight.
Excavator split bushing shims: Machinery owners. Niche, but a repeat-buy part with little local competition to check.
Skid steer tree saw: Machinery attachment, high ticket. A dealer-style sale, not an add-on.
Battery fluid transfer pump: Machinery and farm owners refuelling from drums. Mid-price, decent add-on for the heavy-gear crowd.
Touchless heavy machinery wash: Consumable, so customers rebuy. Fits machinery and trailer owners; liquid shipping needs checking.
POSTA solo post-setting tool: An Aussie brand already doing this. Shows an Aussie tradie tool can sell in the US too.
Rot-proof steel fence posts: Fencing materials, heavy and bulky. A supply business, not an add-on.
Pump-free battery sprayer: Rural and acreage owners. Mid-price, ships OK, different use from straps.
Shock-absorbing framing hammers: Carpenters and framers. Premium tool brand play, not a load-restraint add-on.
Pro framer tool belt: Carpenters. Premium, would need a brand distribution deal.
Holsta adjustable tool belt: Every tradie wears a belt. Light to ship and an easy tradie gift item next to straps.
Gripping tool roll and micro wrench: Mechanics and tradies, but small traffic and already sold in AU.
Magnetic tool holders: Cheap and light, but Bunnings undercuts it.
Modular tool organisers: Already sold in AU with patents. Not worth chasing.
Chain-driven offset extension: Mechanics and tradies, small and light. US interest is fading.
Coated step drill bits: Consumable tradie item, but Bunnings sells cheap versions.
90\u00b0 precision track saw guide: Carpenters and DIY builders. Mid-price; the brand already sells on Amazon AU.
Precision oil-based marker (Precisq): Every tradie uses markers and rebuys them. Tiny, cheap to post, perfect cart add-on with straps.
Precision-tip quick-dry marker: Same as above: a consumable add-on that brings repeat orders.
Multi-size marking scriber: Carpenters and fabricators. Small and light; good low-cost add-on.
MeasurePro tape, laser and level in one: Already sold cheaply in AU. Skip.
Reekon T1R hybrid measuring tool: Premium gadget for carpenters. Would need a distribution deal with the brand.
Moasure 2 Pro area measurer: Landscapers, fencers and concreters quoting jobs. Premium brand, likely already in AU.
Laser tape measure ruler: Similar products already cheap in AU.
Automatic wire stripper: Electricians and scrap recyclers. Higher ticket, different buyer from straps.
Tool-free LED strip and wire connectors: Ute and caravan owners wiring lights. Cheap consumable add-on that suits your ute crowd.
DIY pipe threading tool: Plumbers and DIY. Check AU thread standards first.
Welding gear and hoods: Welders and fabricators. Established US brand; distribution deal rather than white label.
Custom welding hoods: Welders who like custom gear. Brand and design play.
Metal repair glue (cold weld): Farmers, mechanics and ute owners fixing things on the fly. Chemical shipping rules apply.
Laser rust cleaner: Big-ticket machine for fabricators. A different business.
Low-temperature metal repair rods: Cheap add-on for the fix-it-yourself crowd. Quality needs testing.
Cabinet door hanging jig: Cabinet makers and renovators. Small and light; current seller ships slowly to AU.
Solo door hanging tool: Carpenters and builders hanging doors alone. Not sold in the US yet, only Europe.
Door lock installation kit: Carpenters and handymen. Small and light; check AU lock sizes.
Contour gauge with lock: Floor layers and tilers. Cheap add-on; Bunnings has basic versions.
Self-adhesive floor transition strip: Renovators. Cheap, but Bunnings sells strips.
Diamond hole saw for tile and glass: Tilers and plumbers. Consumable, but Bunnings sells them.
Stainless plasterboard patch clips: Only works as part of a repair kit.
Heavy-duty adhesive wall hooks: DIY home buyer, not your customer.
Liquid Rubber deck and roof sealant: Ad has run 936 days. Homeowners and caravan owners; liquid freight needs checking.
Deck stain brush pole: Homeowners and deck builders. Light and cheap to post.
Composite decking: Building material supplied through dealers. A different business.
Solar automatic gate opener: Rural and acreage owners who tow and haul. Mid-to-high ticket, check AU electrical rules.
Custom-moulded earplugs: Tradies on loud sites. Brand already in AU.
Stylish safety glasses: An AU tradie brand already owns this.
Rechargeable work headlamp: Every tradie and ute owner needs one. Light, cheap to post, a good add-on and gift item.
Wearable Bluetooth speaker for site: Tradies on sites that ban earbuds. Mid-price, check site safety rules.
Pitch Hopper roof tool: Roofers and Christmas-light installers. Niche; check AU working-at-heights rules.
Steel glove clamp for tool belts: Tiny, cheap to post, impulse add-on. Same tradie who buys straps for the ute; easy bundle or checkout upsell.
Steel-hook heavy-duty work suspenders: Same buyer, same 'built tough, won't let go' story as a good ratchet strap. Webbing and steel hooks: likely the same factory type as his straps.
DIY spray foam insulation kit: Different business from straps: heavy, hazardous freight and a slower sale. Only worth it if he wants a building-materials line.
Merino work socks with 10-year guarantee: Repeat buy (socks wear out) and a real reason for customers to come back. Light and flat, so very cheap to post.
Cooling hi-vis sun work shirt: Fits an Aussie summer perfectly. Apparel means sizes and returns, which is a different headache from straps.
Adjustable door hinge mortise jig: Small, light, and fits with the door tools already on the list. A carpenter's product rather than a ute buyer's.
15\" curved reciprocating saw blade: Consumable, so blades get rebought. Very cheap to post. Weak brand story on its own; better as part of a bigger tool range.
4-way panel glue-up clamp: For cabinet makers and woodworkers, not ute buyers. Heavier steel, so check freight.
Angle-grinder drill bit sharpener: Cheap, light add-on for any tradie order. Low price means low profit on its own; use it as an upsell.
LockNFlate pro retractable air and water: Proof an Aussie workshop brand can sell to US tradies on Facebook. The same route he could take with straps into the US.
